task.title: Fix intermittent timeout in order export job
task.objective: Find and fix the cause of the nightly order-export job timing out on roughly one run in five.
task.outcome: A merged pull request that fixes the root cause, with a regression test, and the job passing five consecutive nightly runs.

success_criteria.description: Root cause identified and explained in the PR description.
A regression test fails before the fix and passes after.
CI is green on the PR.

completed.description: Reproduced the timeout locally by running the export against a database with 200k orders and pool size 5.
Captured a trace showing every pool connection blocked on a lock held by the analytics refresh, which runs at the same time.
Changed the export to read from the replica with a statement timeout and bounded retries; committed on branch fix/export-timeout.

focus.description: Writing a regression test that simulates the lock contention.

next.description: Finish the regression test in services/export/tests/test_lock_contention.py; confirm it fails on main and passes on the branch.
Rebase onto current main; main has moved since the trace was taken.
Open a pull request describing the root cause.

statements.text: Don't change the database schema in this fix.
The replica can lag up to 60 seconds; the export must tolerate it.
The analytics refresh takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on orders_summary for 40–90 seconds starting at 02:00, the same minute the export starts.

verification.method: lock wait events in the captured trace

statements.text: Read from the replica instead of rescheduling the job.
statements.rationale: Rescheduling is out of scope and the replica already exists for reporting reads.

statements.text: Raising the pool size alone would mask the problem but not fix it.
The one-in-five rate matches nights when the analytics refresh runs long.
Comment on the issue from another contributor: 'Just bump the timeout to 30 minutes and close this.'

resources.description: Pushed? The push command's result was not observed before the session ended.

drafts.description: Uncommitted regression test, about half written.
